Subject: Post-call: MedWell eval scope, dataset format & scoring agenda

Hi Samira — thanks again for today's demo and for walking us through the clinical triage use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before Ben and Marcus start the eval onboarding:

1) Primary objective: measure model accuracy and hallucination rate on intake triage summaries (short clinical notes + patient intent).
2) Target metrics: Top-1 intent accuracy, hallucination incidents per 1k tokens, and a binary safety flag recall for high-risk intents.
3) Recommended initial models to evaluate: Redwood-2B-quant (cost-friendly), Redwood-13B-rt (latency-balanced), and a Llama2-13B q4 variant (baseline comparison).
4) Data we need from you: a 500–1,000-row sample CSV with columns: "note_id", "raw_note", "expected_intent", "safety_label". We discussed synthetic redaction for PHI — perfect.
5) Scoring: we propose exact-match for intent label, custom regex checks for hallucination triggers, and a human review pool for edge cases.

I've attached an example sample and a prompt-set template (simple JSONL) that our eval harness expects. Ben will follow up with the benchmark link and a proposed scoring rubric.

Next call: 30-minute technical onboarding to finalize dataset ingestion and run the first batch (we suggested Mon 1/19; please confirm).

Thanks,

Thanks for the great call — quick technical notes from my side:

- Latency profiles: Redwood-2B-quant should be ~120–180ms p95 on a dedicated 1xA10g-like instance with our quantized runtime. Redwood-13B-rt typically sits in the 250–380ms p95 range depending on sequence lengths. Llama2-13B q4 will be slower in our infra (roughly 300–450ms p95) but is useful as an open-model baseline.
- Scoring harness: we'll run an automated pipeline that computes intent accuracy (exact match), confusion matrix, hallucination heuristic counts (we'll share the regex list), and a sampling queue for human review. We'll surface both aggregate metrics and per-note failure traces in the Redwoods Console report.
- For safety labeling, binary high-risk recall is fine for the first phase; we can add multi-class recall in phase 2 if the SME wants that depth.

I posted the initial benchmark harness link here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3CdE-example-benchmarking (read-only). The doc includes the runner command, expected CSV schema, and the prompt-set example.

Attaching the redwood_eval_guidelines.pdf which outlines our scoring heuristics and human-review workflow.

Hi all — dropping the exact schema here and a short rubric (also uploaded to the Drive):

CSV rules:
- Encoding: UTF-8
- Delimiter: comma (,); enclosed by double quotes if fields contain commas
- Columns required: note_id, raw_note, expected_intent, safety_label, created_at (ISO 8601)
- Optional columns: patient_age_bucket, clinician_notes
- Max single file size: 200MB; please gzip larger batches and we will accept .csv.gz via our secure ingest link.

Human-review rubric (short):
- Reviewer role: internal Redwood contractors with healthcare experience for phase 1; customer adjudication accepted for final labels (you can supply adjudicated gold set).
- Instructions: for each sampled response, mark IntentCorrect (yes/no), HallucinationPresent (yes/no), SafetyEscalationNeeded (yes/no), and free-text reasoning if flagged.
- Sample size for review: we recommend 200 sampled errors or low-confidence responses, whichever comes first.

I uploaded: medwell_eval_dataset_sample.csv, medwell_prompt_set_v1.jsonl, and a short human_review_rubric.md to the Drive folder. I also added an ingestion checklist and a one-click job command to run the first 500-row batch on Redwood.

I'll set up the secure ingest link and share the DocuSign for the trial Eval Terms (standard NDA + data handling addendum) — expect those links in the morning.

—Marcus
